tier_rationale: as-assigned (Tier 1 'Legitimate analytical testing lab' per seed). Testides is a Canadian analytical testing lab providing HPLC purity, mass spectrometry, endotoxin (LAL), microbial, heavy metals, and residual solvents testing services for peptides, small molecules, nootropics, and dietary supplement ingredients sent in by third-party customers. The retail-product schema fields (per_mg_price, dose, list_price_usd, sale_price_usd, out_of_stock, age_gate, on_site_reviews, etc.) are categorically uncertain because Testides does not sell peptides — they test peptides for paying customers (research vendors, pharmaceutical companies, individual buyers verifying purity). The lab's catalog (85 testable compounds via /api/peptides/public), service categories (HPLC purity, MS, microbial, endotoxin, heavy metals, residual solvents, custom analysis), turnaround times (24-48 hours fast option, 5-10 business days standard), payment methods (Stripe credit/debit, Interac e-Transfer, Wise), CAD pricing currency, ISO 17025 alignment, Toronto ON location, Canada+USA shipping coverage, and React/Vite/Cloudflare tech stack ARE captured. Field completion ratio computed at 0.6379 (37/58 leaf fields non-uncertain) → 'partial' per Rule 17. Tier remains 1 per seed: this is real category infrastructure (the testing lab serious researchers use to verify vendor claims), not a downgradeable position.

uncertainty_notes: fetch_status='partial' per Rule 17 (computed field_completion_ratio 37/58 = 0.6379, in 0.40-0.69 partial band). REASON FOR PARTIAL: Testides is a Canadian analytical testing lab — it sells testing services, not peptides. The Pillar A schema is built around peptide-vendor retail commerce (SKUs, dose, per-mg pricing, list_price, sale_price, on-site reviews, age-gate, COA-hosting-as-product-trust-signal); applying it to a service-only B2B/B2C testing lab leaves many retail-shaped fields as legitimately 'uncertain' rather than fabricated. Computed ratio 37/58 = 0.6379 (just under the 0.70 threshold for 'ok', firmly within the 0.40-0.69 'partial' band). ARTIFACTS: 5 saved in 03_raw_fetches/testides/ — homepage.md (composite of HTML shell + JS-bundle string constants extracted via grep -oE; the React SPA renders empty <div id=root> from curl, so the user-visible content lives client-side in the /assets/index-C7iQRKk4.js bundle and was extracted there per Rule 6 — quotes still grep-match because the bundle strings ARE the rendered text), catalog_peptides.md (full JSON response from public /api/peptides/public listing 85 testable compounds), source_homepage.md (the JS-bundle string-constant extract used for tech-stack inferences), response_headers.md (Cloudflare-server response headers from /, /api/peptides/public, and /api/client/service-agreement/download), tos.md (terms-of-service route — returns SPA shell only; full TOS body auth-gated). Those would be re-pasted SKU rows that would create false equivalence with retail vendors and fail Rule 1. RECOMMENDATION FOR OPERATOR: Testides is a service vendor, not a product vendor. They are infrastructure for the peptide-research category — the lab buyers use to verify a retail vendor's purity claims. They should be tracked as a category-trust signal (i.e., 'which retail vendors publish Testides COAs?' is itself a Pillar A signal across other vendor profiles), not benchmarked against retail competitors. Pricing intelligence (Pillar C) cannot be generated from this profile because there are no SKUs. Customer-acquisition channel intelligence (Pillar B) is light because the JS bundle exposes no blog, no testimonials, no influencer relationships, no off-site social signals — they appear to acquire via direct word-of-mouth in pharma/research institutional networks plus the Reddit-citation channel noted in the seed CSV ('Y (Reddit)').
